hero.title: Welcome to “Championship 960” — the largest chess experiment of our time!
hero.p1: We asked ourselves: what if we removed the memorized openings from chess, but still gave players complete control over their starting positions?
hero.p2: What if, before the game began, each player — like a general before a battle — chose their own piece placement?
hero.p3: Our project is an attempt to find the answer. We will challenge the powerful chess engine Stockfish to play nearly a million games in a new format to uncover the deepest secrets of the opening stages of the game.

step1.title: 960 unique setups
step1.text: There are 960 opening setups that comply with the rules of Chess960.

step2.title: White chooses
step2.text: Before the game, White chooses any of the 960 setups for their pieces.

step3.title: Black chooses
step3.text: Black independently chooses any of the 960 setups for their pieces.

step4.title: The game begins!
step4.text: This is more than just chance. It is a conscious strategic choice that determines the entire subsequent nature of the game.

advantages.title: Key Advantages: A New Era of Chess

a1.title: Freedom from opening memorization
a1.subtitle: Advantage over classical chess
a1.text: In modern chess, the outcome often depends on deep theory analyzed by computers. Our format breaks this cycle: every game is unique from move one.
a1.result: The winner is the player with deeper understanding and creativity, not the one with the best memory.

a2.title: Strategic choice, not random chance
a2.subtitle: Advantage over Chess960
a2.text: Fischer Random removes theory but forces random positions. We go further: players fully control their starting setup to match their style and intent.
a2.result: You don’t adapt to circumstances — you create them.

a3.title: Inexhaustible depth of analysis
a3.text: 960 positions for White × 960 for Black = 921,600 unique starting combinations — a new universe of chess to explore.

academic.title: Academic Research
academic.text: Create a fundamental database to analyze chess principles — piece values, central control, and pawn structures — on an unprecedented scale.

strongest.title: Identifying the strongest positions
strongest.text: Statistically determine which setups are objectively best for White and Black — and whether universal choices exist or depend on the opponent.

openingTheory.title: Creating a new opening theory
openingTheory.text: Build a fresh, data-driven opening theory for this format, free from historical overlays.

principles.title: Evaluating fundamental principles
principles.text: Test long-held dogmas — importance of the center, the power of the bishop pair, and more — across diverse positions.

gems.title: Finding “hidden gems”
gems.text: Discover asymmetrical or seemingly weak setups that prove formidable in the hands of a prepared player.

scale.title: Scale of Research
scale.b3: Every White position plays against every Black position.
scale.b4: A total of 921,600 unique games will be played!
scale.note: This is one of the most ambitious computational experiments in the history of chess.

concluding.p: Join us on this fascinating journey to the very foundations of chess strategy. Follow our updates to discover the secrets hidden beyond the familiar first move.
concluding.title: The Future of Chess Starts Here.

landing.tagline: Your rules. Your strategy. Your chess.

problem.title: Why do chess need a reboot?
problem.text1: At the top level, classical chess increasingly becomes a memory contest. Players spend thousands of hours memorizing openings; the real fight often starts only around move 15–20.
problem.text2: Fischer Random (Chess960) helps, but the starting position is random — you must adapt to what you’re given instead of choosing on purpose.

solution.title: Time to become the General!
solution.text: In Chess960v2 you are the General. You choose the starting setup to match your style and idea, combining freedom from memorization with full control.

bullets.attack: Want a fast attack? Pick an aggressive setup.
bullets.draw: Need safety? Choose a solid defensive scheme.
bullets.surprise: Want to surprise? Hundreds of unconventional choices await.

solution.note: Why ‘v2’? Not just ‘version 2’, but a symbol of a new degree of freedom — a virtually boundless canvas for creativity.

tournament.title: Proving ground: year‑long Stockfish 15.1 event
tournament.text1: To showcase the format’s depth, we run a year‑long tournament: Stockfish 15.1 plays itself from many starting setups — NNUE disabled by default to highlight pure strategy.
tournament.text2: Time control: 3 seconds per move. This yields dynamic games, about three rounds per day, finishing in a year.

hardware.title: Our hardware
hardware.note: This setup sustains 16 concurrent matches without performance loss.

future.title: From this tournament to a broader revolution
future.text1: This is just the beginning. We aim to make it regular and form leagues: Elite, Division 1, Division 2, and beyond.
future.text2: The ultimate goal: a server where people play Chess960v2 vs humans, and this site helps analyze and select starting setups for your style.

creator.title: A project born from love for the game
creator.text1: I’m Nikolai Lavrenov. I love chess, but dislike when opening prep suppresses creativity. I built this to bring strategy back from move one.
creator.text2: Open source and community‑backed. With your help we’ll run new leagues with deeper time controls.
